Sunday, November 23, 1952
Dear Femily,
We've had a busy time in Manila since our arrival lest
Monday afternoon. Our plans are sufficiently jelled now to permit
of en itinerary which we hope cen be followed. It follows:

We are both looking forward to this last lap in our trip
around the world, especially our stops at Houston, St. Louis and
Louisville.
Ordinarily weld look forward to that projected stay et
Honolulu but I honestly think if it weren't for some business there
thet we'd gallop right throush.
Debby has been overseas since Sept-
ember 5th living out of a suitcase, weering the same dresses, sleeping
in strange places end eating food which, with the exception of Paris
and Switzerland has not always been too good. I had one week at home
in October so it's that much easier for me.
However, Debby found
an old rilipino shell collector here which is for her what a circus
is for a 12 year old boy.
Last night we had dinner with some old friends at the Jai
Lai.
It was a wonderful dinner served way up high with the games
going on down below and a boy standing at the elbow to place your
bets.
Debby didn't do so well because she wasn't cuite as scientific
as I. I bet on a bounding Basque named Pavlo, because his name re-
minded me of that dreadful stuff which our girls feed to their unsus-
pecting, trustful babies. He not only won but he was a long shot,
so I ceme out ahead on the evening by a few paltry pesos.
I had two business objectives in Manila, neither of which
has been wholly attained or completely lost.
Furthermore, that status
may obtain when we leave but at least I've done my best end each
situation is at least clarified if nothing more.
Furthermore, nothing
could be accomplished by staying longer.
Will try to write again from somewhere along the line.
All the best,
H. M. B.
